title: AxiBridge How-To
summary: Use this guide to navigate every core workflow in AxiBridge.
content:
AxiBridge helps you ingest **Guild Wars 2 arcdps logs**, analyze combat performance, and share outputs with your squad.

## ![Map](icon:list-tree) How to use this guide

- Use the **Guide Map** on the left to jump by area.
- Use the **breadcrumbs** at the top to move up/down the hierarchy.
- Start with **Getting Started** for initial setup, then explore **Dashboard**, **Stats View**, and **Sharing**.
- For web hosting see **GitHub Web Reports** or **Cloudflare R2**; for local parsing see **Elite Insights**.

> ![Tip](icon:check) Tip: Jump to **Troubleshooting** at any time if something isn't working.

children.title: Getting Started
children.summary: Initial setup, first upload flow, and what to expect.
children.content:
## ![Check](icon:check) Setup checklist

- Set your **Log Directory** to your `arcdps.cbtlogs` folder — see **Log Directory** below if you're not sure where it is.
- Optionally add your **dps.report token** for a persistent identity on uploaded logs.
- Set up **Discord** or a **web report host** (GitHub Pages or Cloudflare R2) if you plan to share outputs.

## ![Upload](icon:upload) First ingest workflow

1. Set your log directory and enable **Watch Folder** in the sidebar.
2. Play a fight in WvW — ArcDPS writes a `.zevtc` file when the fight ends.
3. AxiBridge detects the new file and queues it automatically.
4. Watch the status badge: `QUE → PEN → uploading → LOG`.
5. Expand the fight card to view the dps.report link and computed stats.

## ![Error](icon:error) Common first-run checks

- No logs appearing? See **Log Directory** for path help.
- Uploads failing? Check your dps.report token and webhook URL in Settings.
- Stats delayed? Wait for the background worker — a progress bar appears while it computes.
- Want more accurate WvW data? See **Elite Insights** to install the local parser.

children.title: Log Directory
children.summary: Where arcdps saves fight logs and how to find the right path.
children.content:
## ![Folder](icon:folder) Where ArcDPS saves logs

ArcDPS writes `.zevtc` files to a folder inside your Guild Wars 2 documents directory. The path depends on how you run GW2.

### ![Check](icon:check) Windows — native install

```
C:\Users\<YourName>\Documents\Guild Wars 2\addons\arcdps\arcdps.cbtlogs
```

Replace `<YourName>` with your Windows username.

### ![Check](icon:check) Windows — Steam install

GW2 still writes logs to your Documents folder regardless of Steam:

```
C:\Users\<YourName>\Documents\Guild Wars 2\addons\arcdps\arcdps.cbtlogs
```

### ![Check](icon:check) Linux — Steam + Proton

Proton redirects the Documents folder into the game's compatibility data directory. The typical path is:

```
~/.steam/steam/steamapps/compatdata/1284210/pfx/drive_c/users/steamuser/Documents/Guild Wars 2/addons/arcdps/arcdps.cbtlogs
```

If your Steam library is on a secondary drive, replace `~/.steam/steam` with your library path (e.g. `/mnt/data/SteamLibrary`).

> ![Tip](icon:check) Tip: `1284210` is GW2's Steam App ID — it doesn't change between accounts or installs.

## ![Settings](icon:settings) Setting the path in AxiBridge

1. Click the **folder icon** in the sidebar, or open **Settings → General → Log Directory**.
2. Browse to the `arcdps.cbtlogs` folder and confirm.
3. Enable **Watch Folder** in the sidebar so new logs are picked up automatically.

## ![Error](icon:error) If ArcDPS creates subfolders

Some ArcDPS configurations split logs into per-character or per-map subfolders inside `arcdps.cbtlogs`. If that's the case, point AxiBridge at the specific subfolder you want to watch, or check your ArcDPS config for a way to disable subfolder splitting.

children.title: dps.report Token
children.summary: Get a user token so your uploads are tied to your account.
children.content:
## ![Upload](icon:upload) What the token does

By default, AxiBridge uploads logs to dps.report anonymously. Adding your **user token** ties all uploads to your dps.report account, which means:

- Logs appear in your dps.report upload history.
- Links don't expire as quickly.
- You can manage or delete uploads from the dps.report website.

The token is optional — AxiBridge works fine without it.

## ![Link](icon:link) Getting your token

1. Go to [dps.report](https://dps.report) in your browser.
2. Click **Login** and authenticate with your Guild Wars 2 account.
3. After login, open your account menu (top right) and navigate to **Settings** or **Token**.
4. Copy the token string.

## ![Settings](icon:settings) Adding the token to AxiBridge

1. Open **Settings → General**.
2. Paste your token into the **dps.report User Token** field.
3. Save — future uploads will be attributed to your account.

> ![Tip](icon:check) Tip: The token is stored locally and never shared. You can clear it from the same Settings field at any time.

children.title: Discord Webhook
children.summary: Create a webhook and connect it so AxiBridge can post fight summaries.
children.content:
## ![Plug](icon:plug) What a webhook does

A Discord webhook is a URL that lets AxiBridge post messages directly into a channel — no bot invite needed. Each fight upload can automatically send an embed or image summary to your squad's server.

## ![List](icon:list-tree) Step-by-step setup

### ![Settings](icon:settings) 1. Create the webhook in Discord

1. Open Discord and go to the channel you want AxiBridge to post in.
2. Click the **⚙ Edit Channel** gear icon.
3. Go to **Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook**.
4. Give it a name (e.g. `AxiBridge`) and optionally set an avatar.
5. Click **Copy Webhook URL**.

### ![Plug](icon:plug) 2. Add the webhook in AxiBridge

1. Open **Settings → Discord**.
2. Click **Add Webhook** and paste the URL.
3. Give it a label so you can identify it (e.g. the channel name).
4. Save.

### ![Settings](icon:settings) 3. Choose notification mode

- **Embed** — a rich formatted card with stats, links, and player breakdown.
- **Image** — a visual screenshot; better when the embed layout feels too dense.
- **Tiled** — multiple image panels for detailed breakdowns.

### ![Check](icon:check) 4. Test it

Upload any `.zevtc` file and watch your Discord channel — you should see a post appear within a few seconds of the upload completing.

## ![Error](icon:error) Troubleshooting

- **No post in Discord** — verify the webhook URL is correct (paste it in a browser; it should return a JSON object).
- **Webhook deleted** — if the channel or webhook was removed in Discord, create a new one and update AxiBridge.
- **Posts stopped** — Discord rate-limits webhooks; avoid posting more than ~30 messages per minute.

children.title: First Fight Walkthrough
children.summary: End-to-end: from a WvW fight to seeing stats in AxiBridge.
children.content:
## ![Rocket](icon:rocket) What happens end-to-end

Here's what AxiBridge does from the moment ArcDPS finishes writing a log to the moment you see stats.

## ![List](icon:list-tree) Step-by-step

### ![Check](icon:check) 1. ArcDPS writes the log

When a WvW fight ends, ArcDPS finalizes the `.zevtc` file in your `arcdps.cbtlogs` folder. This can take a few seconds after the fight.

### ![Folder](icon:folder) 2. AxiBridge detects the file

With **Watch Folder** on, AxiBridge sees the new file immediately and creates a fight card showing `QUE`.

### ![Upload](icon:upload) 3. Upload to dps.report

The file is queued and uploaded (up to 3 concurrent uploads). Status moves from `QUE → PEN → ...` (uploading). Once complete the dps.report link is saved.

### ![Bar-chart](icon:bar-chart) 4. Stats calculation

AxiBridge fetches the parsed EI JSON from dps.report (or runs Elite Insights locally if installed). The fight card shows `CAL` while stats are computed, then flips to `LOG`.

### ![Dashboard](icon:dashboard) 5. Fight card is ready

Expand the fight card to see:
- dps.report link
- Duration, squad DPS, downs/deaths
- Quick share buttons for Discord and web report

### ![Activity](icon:activity) 6. Stats View

Switch to **Stats View** to see this fight (and any others in the session) aggregated. Use the log selector to narrow or expand the range.

## ![Check](icon:check) Expected timeline

| Stage | Typical time |
|---|---|
| ArcDPS finalizes log | 1–5s after fight ends |
| AxiBridge detects + queues | < 1s |
| Upload to dps.report | 5–30s depending on file size |
| Stats fetch + calculation | 2–10s |
| Total from fight end to `LOG` | ~10–45s |

children.title: Dashboard
children.summary: Operational view for ingest, statuses, and per-fight actions.
children.content:
## ![Live](icon:activity) Live Operations Surface

The Dashboard is your command center for managing logs and active uploads. It provides a real-time view of your current session's activity.

## ![Watch](icon:folder) Watch Folder

The **Watch Folder** toggle (sidebar header) auto-detects new `.zevtc` files as ArcDPS creates them:

- **On** — any new file saved to your log directory is immediately queued.
- **Off** — logs are only added when you manually use the file picker.

To add files without Watch Folder, click the folder icon in the sidebar to open the file picker.

## ![Card](icon:file) Anatomy of a Fight Card

Each log appears as a card with rich metadata and status indicators:

- **Status badges**:
  - ![Queued](icon:clock) `QUE` — queued, waiting for an upload slot.
  - ![Pending](icon:upload) `PEN` — pending; a slot will open shortly.
  - ![Uploading](icon:globe) `...` — uploading to dps.report.
  - ![Calc](icon:bar-chart) `CAL` — calculating statistics (local EI parsing).
  - ![Success](icon:check) `LOG` — success, ready to view and share.
  - ![Error](icon:error) `ERR` — failed; hover for details, use Retry to re-queue.

- **Metrics preview** (once processed):
  - ![Time](icon:clock) **Duration** — fight length.
  - ![DPS](icon:activity) **Squad DPS** — total group output.
  - ![Downs](icon:error) **Downs/Deaths** — quick survival check.

## ![Batch](icon:layers) Batch Operations

Manage multiple logs at once:

1. **Select** — click the checkboxes on valid cards.
2. **Bulk actions** (bottom bar):
   - ![Upload](icon:upload) **Upload Selected** — retry or force-upload to web.
   - ![Copy](icon:file) **Copy Links** — grab all dps.report links at once.
   - ![Open](icon:globe) **Open** — launch selected logs in the browser.

## ![Tips](icon:check) Best practices

- Keep Watch Folder on during active raid sessions so every fight is captured automatically.
- Expand a fight card to access per-fight share actions and the screenshot export.
- If a log is stuck on `ERR`, hover the badge for the failure reason, then use Retry.

children.title: Stats View
children.summary: Deep analysis of aggregated session performance.
children.content:
## ![Stats](icon:bar-chart) Deep Session Analysis

Stats View aggregates all selected logs into a single **session-level** report — ideal for spotting patterns across multiple fights.

## ![Select](icon:layers) Choosing which logs to include

Use the **log selector** at the top of Stats View to choose the date range or specific fights to include. Only logs within that selection feed the aggregated stats. Narrowing the range is useful for comparing early vs late in a raid session.

## ![Chart](icon:activity) Analysis Sections

The sidebar gives you access to 16+ detailed breakdowns:

- **Core**:
  - ![Home](icon:dashboard) **Overview** — high-level trends (DPS, Cleanses, Strips).
  - ![Fight](icon:activity) **Fight Breakdown** — table of every fight with duration and success status.
  - ![Top](icon:bar-chart) **Top Players** — MVP rankings based on your configured weights.
- **Combat**:
  - ![Sword](icon:activity) **Offense / Defense / Support** — traditional role breakdowns.
  - ![Heal](icon:heart) **Healing** — outgoing healing distribution (requires Elite Insights).
- **Technical**:
  - ![Buff](icon:arrow-up) **Boons / Buffs** — uptime and generation stats.
  - ![Condi](icon:droplet) **Conditions** — incoming and outgoing pressure.
  - ![Time](icon:clock) **Timeline** — visual progression across the session.
  - ![Skill](icon:sliders) **Skill Usage** — rotation efficiency, casts, and cancels (requires Elite Insights).

## ![Nav](icon:dashboard) Navigation tips

- **Search bar** — filter by player name or account to isolate individuals.
- **Camera icon** — capture the current section as an image for Discord sharing.
- For large sessions, stats run in a background worker; a progress bar appears while computing.
- Some sections (Healing, Skill Usage) require **Elite Insights** — see the Elite Insights guide if they are empty.

children.title: Sharing
children.summary: Output workflows for Discord, screenshots, and web reports.
children.content:
## ![Share](icon:globe) Output options

- **Discord embed** — rich formatted card posted directly to a channel via webhook.
- **Discord image** — visual screenshot posted to a webhook; better for dense tables.
- **Stats screenshot** — manually export the current Stats View section as an image.
- **Web report** — publish a persistent, browsable site via GitHub Pages or Cloudflare R2.

## ![Discord](icon:plug) Discord quick setup

1. In Discord, open **Channel Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook**.
2. Copy the webhook URL.
3. In AxiBridge, go to **Settings → Discord** and paste the URL.
4. Choose your notification mode — **Embed** for rich cards, **Image** for a visual summary.
5. Test by uploading a log and confirming the post appears in your Discord channel.

## ![Screenshot](icon:file) Screenshot export

- Open **Stats View** and navigate to any section.
- Click the **camera icon** at the top-right of the section to capture the visible content.
- The image is generated and can be posted directly to Discord or saved locally.

## ![Select](icon:mouse-pointer) Choosing the right output

- Use **Discord embed** for rapid in-session summaries your squad sees immediately.
- Use **Discord image** when the data is table-heavy and the embed layout doesn't fit well.
- Use **web reports** for historical links, full session browsing, and commander archives.
- Use **screenshots** for one-click visual shares without needing a webhook configured.

## ![Check](icon:shield) Reliability checks

- Validate your webhook URL before high-volume posting — paste it in a browser and confirm it returns a JSON response.
- Confirm the web publish URL resolves after build (GitHub Pages takes 30–60s).
- If output looks stale, re-run with fresh logs and check build status in the GitHub section.

children.title: Settings & Integrations
children.summary: Central control for behavior, metrics, visuals, and integrations.
children.content:
## ![Config](icon:settings) Configuration Center

Control every aspect of AxiBridge, from visual themes to deep metric weighting.

## ![Controls](icon:sliders) Key configurations

### ![Theme](icon:palette) General & Appearance
- **Theme** — switch between Classic, Modern, and accessible Contrast modes.
- **Auto-Update** — toggle background checks for new versions.

### ![Connect](icon:plug) Discord Integration
- **Notification Mode** — choose **Embed** (rich card) or **Image** (visual summary).
- **Split Enemies by Team** — in **Settings → Discord Embed - Summary Sections**, enable this to split enemy summary and class breakdown by `Team <id>` across Embed, Image, and Tiled notifications.
- **Webhooks** — set separate destinations for automated upload alerts vs manual shares.

### ![Stats](icon:bar-chart) Stats Engine
- **MVP Weights** — customize how the Top Player score is calculated (e.g., weight Revives higher than DPS).
- **Disruption Tracking** — count CC by **number of hits** or **duration** of breakbar damage.

### ![Parser](icon:database) Parser Settings
- **Elite Insights** — install the local EI parser for precise WvW metrics, offline support, and no file size limits. See the **Elite Insights** guide for full setup steps.
- **Force dps.report only** — disables local EI parsing and routes all logs through dps.report.

### ![Data](icon:database) Data Management
- **Clear dps.report cache** — removes locally cached parse results to free space or fix display glitches.
- **Export / Import Settings** — save your full configuration to a file for backup or migration.

children.title: GitHub Web Reports
children.summary: Hosted report pipeline using GitHub repositories and Pages.
children.content:
## ![Web](icon:github) Web Report Hosting

AxiBridge integrates directly with GitHub Pages to publish your reports to the web. Reports are stored as files in a GitHub repository and served as a static website — free, permanent, and shareable by URL.

**Best for:** squads who want free hosting, don't mind public repos, and are comfortable with GitHub.

## ![Rocket](icon:rocket) Workflow Overview

1. ![Link](icon:link) **Connect** — link your GitHub account to AxiBridge.
2. ![Repo](icon:folder) **Repository** — choose where to store your report files.
3. ![Theme](icon:palette) **Customize** — pick a visual theme and upload a squad logo.
4. ![Globe](icon:globe) **Publish** — every time you upload via the Dashboard, your site updates automatically.

## ![Setup](icon:file) Setup Guide

- **Repositories** — use an existing repo or let AxiBridge create a new private `report-host` for you.
- **Pages** — GitHub Pages turns your repository into a public website. AxiBridge handles the configuration.

## ![Settings](icon:settings) Troubleshooting

- **Auth Errors** — if uploads fail, try reconnecting your account in this tab.
- **Build Delays** — GitHub takes 30–60s to publish changes; check the Build Status indicator.

children.title: Connect & Authorize
children.summary: Authenticate and target the repository for publishing.
children.content:
## ![Steps](icon:list-tree) Step-by-step

### ![Link](icon:link) 1. Start connection in AxiBridge

- Open **Settings → GitHub Web Reports**.
- Click the connect/authenticate action.
- AxiBridge will display a short verification code and a GitHub URL.

### ![Shield](icon:shield) 2. Complete verification on GitHub

- Open the provided GitHub verification page.
- Sign in to your GitHub account if not already.
- Enter the code shown by AxiBridge.
- Approve access when prompted.

After approval, AxiBridge shows a connected state.

### ![Folder](icon:folder) 3. Choose a repository

- Select an existing repository, or
- Create a new one directly from AxiBridge.

For new users, a dedicated repo just for reports is easiest.

### ![Check](icon:check) 4. Confirm repo details

- **Owner** — your GitHub username or org.
- **Repository name** — target repo for report files.
- **Branch** — usually `main`.
- **Pages URL** — the generated website URL used for sharing.

## ![Check](icon:check) First-time validation checklist

- Auth state shows connected.
- Repo is selectable and saved.
- Pages URL appears.
- No error banner in the GitHub section.

## ![Error](icon:error) Common issues

- **Wrong account** — sign out of GitHub in your browser and reconnect.
- **Repo not visible** — check repo permissions and refresh the list.
- **Connection error** — retry auth; the token may be expired or revoked.
- **Pages URL missing** — wait for repo setup to finish, then retry.

children.title: Theme & Branding
children.summary: Set report visuals and keep published branding consistent.
children.content:
## ![Control](icon:sliders) What this section controls

- **Web theme** — visual style, colors, and layout for published reports.
- **Logo** — image shown in the report branding area.
- **Template sync** — ensures the hosted report structure is up to date.

## ![Flow](icon:layers) Recommended workflow

1. Connect GitHub and select a repo first.
2. Choose your theme in AxiBridge.
3. Optionally select a logo file.
4. Apply/sync changes.
5. Wait for build status to complete.
6. Open the Pages URL in a browser and confirm visuals.

## ![Image](icon:file) Logo guidance

- Prefer a clean PNG or SVG with a transparent background.
- Avoid very large files — keep under a few MB.
- If the logo looks stretched, try a square or balanced aspect ratio.

## ![Check](icon:check) How to verify changes

- Build status moves from pending to success.
- Refresh the published URL after the build finishes.
- Confirm theme colors and logo match your selection.

## ![Error](icon:error) If customization doesn't appear

- Re-run apply theme/logo.
- Confirm repo and branch are correct.
- Check build status for errors.
- Hard-refresh the browser (Ctrl+Shift+R) to bypass cached content.

children.title: In-App Report History Viewer
children.summary: Open hosted reports inside AxiBridge using the History tab.
children.content:
## ![Globe](icon:globe) What this feature does

The top-level **History** tab opens your hosted GitHub Pages report site directly inside AxiBridge.

- It lands on your report index page.
- Clicking a fight report stays in the in-app viewer.

## ![List](icon:list-tree) Setup requirements

Before using the History viewer:

1. Go to **Settings → GitHub Web Reports**.
2. Connect GitHub and select a repo.
3. Ensure the **Pages URL** is configured.
4. Publish at least one web report.

If Pages is not configured, the History tab shows a setup prompt.

## ![Error](icon:error) If reports don't appear

- Reopen the History tab.
- Confirm repo, branch, and Pages URL in Settings.
- Verify the GitHub Pages build completed successfully.
- Hard-refresh the embedded page (Ctrl+R) after a fresh publish.

children.title: Cloudflare R2
children.summary: Alternative to GitHub Pages — S3-compatible object storage with no egress fees.
children.content:
## ![Database](icon:database) Cloudflare R2 as a report host

**Cloudflare R2** is an S3-compatible object storage service that AxiBridge can use to publish web reports instead of (or alongside) GitHub Pages.

**Best for:** squads who want private hosting, already use Cloudflare, or need more control over their report URLs.

## ![Rocket](icon:rocket) Advantages over GitHub Pages

- No public GitHub repo required — reports can be private behind a Cloudflare domain.
- No build delay — files are served immediately after upload.
- No file size or bandwidth limits for the free tier (up to 10 GB storage, zero egress fees).
- Custom domain support via Cloudflare DNS.

## ![List](icon:list-tree) What you need

- A free [Cloudflare account](https://cloudflare.com).
- An R2 bucket with public access enabled (or a custom domain pointed at it).
- An R2 API token with read/write permissions.
- The **Account ID**, **Access Key ID**, **Secret Access Key**, **Bucket Name**, and **Public URL** from Cloudflare.

children.title: Bucket Setup
children.summary: Create and configure the R2 bucket AxiBridge will publish to.
children.content:
## ![Database](icon:database) Creating your R2 bucket

### ![Check](icon:check) 1. Create the bucket

1. Log in to the [Cloudflare dashboard](https://dash.cloudflare.com).
2. In the left sidebar, go to **R2 Object Storage**.
3. Click **Create bucket**.
4. Give it a name (e.g. `axibridge-reports`) — this becomes part of your URL if using the default domain.
5. Leave the location as automatic unless you have a preference.
6. Click **Create bucket**.

### ![Globe](icon:globe) 2. Enable public access

R2 buckets are private by default. To serve reports publicly you have two options:

**Option A — Managed public URL (simplest):**
1. Open the bucket in the Cloudflare dashboard.
2. Go to **Settings → Public access**.
3. Enable the **R2.dev subdomain** — this gives you a URL like `https://pub-xxxx.r2.dev`.
4. Copy this URL — you'll need it as the **Public URL** in AxiBridge.

**Option B — Custom domain (recommended for squads):**
1. Go to **Settings → Custom Domains** in the bucket.
2. Add a domain you own and have in Cloudflare DNS (e.g. `reports.yourguild.com`).
3. Cloudflare configures the DNS automatically.
4. Use this domain as the **Public URL** in AxiBridge.

### ![Shield](icon:shield) 3. Configure CORS

AxiBridge may need to read report data in-app. Add a CORS policy to allow this:

1. Go to **Settings → CORS policy** in the bucket.
2. Add a rule allowing `GET` from `*` (or restrict to your domain):

```json
[
  {
    "AllowedOrigins": ["*"],
    "AllowedMethods": ["GET"],
    "AllowedHeaders": ["*"]
  }
]
```

3. Save the policy.

### ![Error](icon:error) If AxiBridge logs `R2 PutBucketCors failed: HTTP 403`

AxiBridge tries to set the CORS rule automatically during a web upload, but a standard **Object Read & Write** R2 API token does not have permission to call `PutBucketCors` — that requires bucket-admin scope. You'll see a warning like:

```
R2 CORS setup failed (HTTP 403 — AccessDenied). The replay viewer may not load in the browser.
```

Fix it one of two ways:

- **Recommended — set CORS manually once.** In the Cloudflare R2 dashboard → bucket → **Settings → CORS**, add an `AllowedOrigin` of your GitHub Pages origin (e.g. `https://<your-user>.github.io`) with `GET` method. Once set, AxiBridge will skip the auto-update on subsequent uploads.
- **Or — use an Admin token.** Recreate the R2 API token with **Admin Read & Write** permissions and re-enter it in Settings. AxiBridge can then maintain CORS automatically.

## ![Check](icon:check) Validation

- Upload a test file manually in the Cloudflare dashboard and open its public URL in a browser.
- If it serves the file, your bucket is ready.

children.title: Connect to AxiBridge
children.summary: Get your R2 credentials and enter them in Settings.
children.content:
## ![Link](icon:link) Getting your R2 credentials

AxiBridge needs four values from Cloudflare to authenticate with R2.

### ![Shield](icon:shield) 1. Find your Account ID

1. Log in to the [Cloudflare dashboard](https://dash.cloudflare.com).
2. Select any domain (or go to **R2 Object Storage** directly).
3. Your **Account ID** appears in the right sidebar or in the URL: `dash.cloudflare.com/<account-id>/r2`.

### ![Key](icon:shield) 2. Create an R2 API token

1. Go to **R2 Object Storage → Manage R2 API tokens**.
2. Click **Create API token**.
3. Set permissions to **Object Read & Write** for your specific bucket (or all buckets).
4. Click **Create API token**.
5. Copy the **Access Key ID** and **Secret Access Key** — the secret is shown only once.

### ![Database](icon:database) 3. Note your bucket name and public URL

- **Bucket name** — the name you gave the bucket (e.g. `axibridge-reports`).
- **Public URL** — the R2.dev subdomain or custom domain you configured in bucket setup.

## ![Settings](icon:settings) Entering credentials in AxiBridge

1. Open **Settings → Cloudflare R2**.
2. Fill in:
   - **Account ID**
   - **Access Key ID**
   - **Secret Access Key**
   - **Bucket Name**
   - **Public URL** (no trailing slash)
3. Save. AxiBridge will use R2 for web report uploads.

## ![Check](icon:check) Validating the connection

- Upload a fight via the Dashboard and check for a public URL in the fight card.
- Open the URL in a browser — the report should load.
- If it fails, double-check the Access Key permissions and that public access is enabled on the bucket.

## ![Error](icon:error) Common issues

- **403 Forbidden on upload** — the API token doesn't have write permissions; recreate it with Object Read & Write.
- **Report URL returns 404** — public access isn't enabled on the bucket, or the public URL has a typo.
- **CORS error in History tab** — add a CORS policy to the bucket as described in **Bucket Setup**.
- **`R2 PutBucketCors failed: HTTP 403 — AccessDenied`** — your API token lacks bucket-admin scope. Either set the CORS rule manually in the dashboard (AllowedOrigin = your GitHub Pages origin, GET) or recreate the token with **Admin Read & Write** permissions. See **Bucket Setup → Configure CORS** for details.
- **Secret Key lost** — R2 only shows the secret once; if lost, delete the old token and create a new one.

children.title: Elite Insights
children.summary: Local parser for precise WvW metrics, offline use, and no file size limits.
children.content:
## ![Parser](icon:database) What Elite Insights does

**Elite Insights (EI)** is an open-source log parser that runs locally on your machine. When installed, AxiBridge routes logs through EI before uploading, producing richer and more accurate combat data.

**Benefits over dps.report-only parsing:**
- No file size limits (dps.report caps very large logs).
- Works offline — parsing doesn't require an internet connection.
- More accurate WvW-specific metrics: precise boon uptime, condition data, and healing stats.
- Unlocks **Skill Usage** and detailed **Healing** sections in Stats View.

## ![Install](icon:rocket) Installing Elite Insights

1. Open **Settings → Parser Settings**.
2. Click **Install / Auto-manage Elite Insights**.
3. AxiBridge downloads and configures EI automatically from GitHub Releases.
4. A status indicator shows the installed version and whether an update is available.

## ![Check](icon:check) Verifying EI is active

- Parser Settings shows **Installed** with a version number.
- When a new log is ingested, the fight card shows `CAL` status while EI processes it locally.
- Stats View sections like **Skill Usage** and precise **Boon** data populate only with EI output.

## ![Update](icon:arrow-up) Keeping EI updated

- Enable **Auto-manage** to let AxiBridge check for and install EI updates automatically.
- Or click **Check for Update** manually in the Parser Settings section.

## ![Error](icon:error) Troubleshooting EI

- **Install fails** — check your internet connection and retry; EI downloads from GitHub Releases.
- **Logs not parsed locally** — confirm EI shows as Installed and **Force dps.report only** is not enabled.
- **Skill Usage / Healing sections empty** — these require a locally parsed log; check the fight card didn't skip to upload-only.
- **Slow parsing on large sessions** — EI is CPU-intensive for big files; progress shows on the fight card during `CAL`.

children.title: Troubleshooting
children.summary: Rapid diagnosis path for ingest, stats, and publish failures.
children.content:
## ![Fix](icon:settings) Solving Common Issues

If something isn't working, start with these checks.

## ![Question](icon:help-circle) Frequently Asked Questions

### ![Folder](icon:folder) Logs aren't showing up?
- Verify your **Log Directory** in Settings matches where ArcDPS saves files (typically `arcdps.cbtlogs`). See **Getting Started → Log Directory** for path help.
- Ensure **Watch Folder** is toggled on in the sidebar if you want auto-import.
- Try adding files manually via the file picker to rule out a watcher issue.

### ![Upload](icon:upload) Uploads failing?
- Check your **dps.report token** in Settings → General.
- Verify your **Discord webhook URL** is valid and the channel still exists (paste it in a browser — it should return JSON).
- If using GitHub, check **Build Status** in Settings → GitHub Web Reports.
- If using R2, verify your API token has read/write permissions and the bucket name is correct.

### ![Chart](icon:bar-chart) Stats missing or incomplete?
- **Healing and Skill Usage** require **Elite Insights** — check Settings → Parser Settings to confirm EI is installed.
- Stats for large sessions may take a moment; a progress indicator appears while the worker computes.
- Narrow the log selector range in Stats View to rule out a data issue with a specific log.

### ![Globe](icon:globe) Web report not updating?
- **GitHub Pages** takes 30–60 seconds to rebuild — wait before refreshing.
- **R2** updates immediately; if stale, check the API token and bucket permissions.
- Hard-refresh your browser (Ctrl+Shift+R) to bypass cached content.

### ![Clock](icon:clock) Logs stuck on QUE or PEN?
- AxiBridge processes up to 3 uploads concurrently; large queues work through in order.
- If a log is stuck indefinitely, restart the app — the queue is persisted and resumes on next launch.

### ![Error](icon:error) Fight card stuck on ERR?
- Hover the `ERR` badge to see the failure reason.
- Use the **Retry** button on the card to re-queue the upload.
- If retries keep failing, the dps.report service may be temporarily down.

### ![Activity](icon:activity) Stats View shows no data?
- Ensure at least one log has reached `LOG` status (fully uploaded and parsed).
- Check the log selector in Stats View — it may be set to a range with no completed logs.

## ![Heart](icon:heart) Getting Help

If you're stuck, join the [Support Discord](https://discord.gg/UjzMXMGXEg).
- Share a screenshot of the error or unexpected behavior.
- Post the relevant fight card status and any tooltip text from the `ERR` badge.
